title: Unified Minimal Surface: Stitch PRD for Chat/Gen/Embed/Rerank with Incremental Launch Checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a compact, unambiguous PRD to launch a minimal but consistent hosted inference surface that covers chat (streaming and non-streaming), single-turn generation/completions, embeddings, and a lightweight rerank endpoint. The goal is a single developer-visible product that is predictable for production apps: consistent request/response semantics, clear backwards-compatible behavior, and operational observability.

Scope: this PRD covers API contracts, behavioral edgecases, rollout strategy, acceptance criteria, QA plans, migration notes for existing hosted endpoint users, and a pre-launch operational checklist. Implementation work is split across runtime (batching, KV caching fallbacks), API layer (SDK changes and compat), console/telemetry (dashboards and tracing), and customer comms.

Non-goals: full multi-model composition flows (retrieval+generation orchestration) and extended multimodal payloads are out of scope for this launch and will be tracked in a follow-up epic.
business_impact_summary: Unifying the minimal surface reduces developer confusion, lowers integration cost for customers adopting multiple capabilities, and enables us to provide consistent SLOs across commonly paired features (e.g., chat+embeddings for retrieval-augmented flows). This directly supports PLG motion and reduces support overhead for endpoint compatibility issues.
api_contract_summary:
Surface summary: four logical endpoints: /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank. Shared semantics: 1) model param selects verified model alias; 2) request headers include x-redwood-mode{sync|stream}; 3) optional context_id for KV caching; 4) token_limit and prompt_truncation_policy are consistent across chat/completions.

Key parameter differences called out:
- chat: messages array of {role, content, metadata}; supports streaming partial deltas and final structured output field.
- completions: prompt string or array, top_k/top_p sampling knobs; no streaming in MVP for prompts > 1e4 tokens.
- embeddings: itemized input array, batching hints via batch_hint param; deterministic hashing for reuse.
- rerank: takes array of candidates and a query; returns scores and stable candidate ids; one-shot operation.

Response shape standardized: top-level fields: request_id, model, latency_ms, timing_breakdown (client-visible tokens | server_tokens | cache_hit), and payload (choices|embeddings|scores). Errors follow new error contract: code, retriable boolean, guidance string.
acceptance_criteria: API contracts implemented for /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank matching the api_contract_summary
Behavioral compatibility: existing hosted customers using current endpoints receive either identical behavior or a documented migration path with automated routing for 30 days
SLOs: p95 latency for single-request chat/completions <= 450ms for region small models, p99 <= 1.2s under synthetic baseline load
Embeddings throughput: batch median per-item compute <= target threshold (release doc) with correctness validated against gold vectors
Rerank stability: reordering for identical inputs is deterministic within model/version; score variance under warm cache < 1e-3
Observability: new per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown available in Console, with alerting for error_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m
SDKs: minimal client change documented, shim available in SDKs to preserve older parameter names for 30 days
Canary: rollout plan executed with safe rollback plan and no customer-facing incidents during canary window
Security: security review signed off; KMS usage for private customer keys where applicable
scope_changes: Initial draft included streaming for completions; removed from MVP to reduce runtime complexity and avoid compatibility regressions
Planned richer structured-output schema pushed to follow-up (tracked as PM-902999)
Expanded rerank feature set (feedback-guided rerank) deferred until after launch to meet Q2 timeline
open_questions: Default truncation policy for chat when both system+user context exceed model token limit — prefer LRU sentence-drop or head-split? (Engineering preferred LRU sentence-drop)
Whether rerank endpoint should return full candidate payload by default or only ids+scores to reduce egress — defaulting to ids+scores for MVP
Do we offer automatic cross-model fallback (e.g., to cheaper quantized variant) at request-time for over-capacity events? (requires billing/consent discussion)
decisions_log: 2026-03-02: Chose unified error contract format (code, retriable, guidance) to reduce SDK parsing complexity - decision by API guild
2026-03-04: Removed streaming from completions MVP to limit kernel deployment surface - decision by runtime and product
2026-03-06: Embeddings will expose deterministic hashing to support cache reuse and deduplication - decision by infra and embeddings team
implementation_notes: Runtime: add light-weight KV prefix caching by context_id and ensure cache diagnostic headers in responses. API: accept legacy param aliases and emit deprecation header. Console: add route-level latency and token cost breakdown. Docs: migration guide with automated 'compat' flag for 30 days. SDKs: expose streaming events for chat and provide a compatibility shim for completions streaming removal.
qa_tests: End-to-end: chat streaming + non-streaming acceptance with long context truncation scenarios
Embeddings: correctness check vs gold vectors for a sample set of 1K inputs and stress test batching behavior
Rerank: determinism test with 1000 repeated requests, cold and warm cache
Compatibility: integration tests for top 20 customers' request shapes captured from production (anonymized)
Chaos: simulate GPU OOM/fallback to quantized variant and validate request-level guidance messages
monitoring_and_slo: Per-route metrics: request_rate, error_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens_generated, cache_hit_rate, avg_tokens_per_req. Alerting: page on error_rate > 1% for >5m or p99 latency spike >2x baseline. Dashboards: token cost heatmap, model-level throughput, canary cohort health. Post-launch 14-day SLA verification: telemetry must prove SLOs hold across >= 95% of regions and customer cohorts.
migration_strategy: Phased migration: 1) deploy new API behind 'v1n' flag; 2) run compatibility shim routing for existing customers for 30 days with traffic mirroring; 3) encourage opt-in via Console toggle and in-product messaging; 4) after 30 days, automatically redirect legacy calls unless customer opts out via enterprise support. Provide a 'compatibility report' for enterprise customers showing any behavioral deltas and recommended config changes.
rollout_plan: Canary cohort (internal + opt-in customers): 5% traffic for 48 hours with elevated telemetry checks
Expanded canary: 25% traffic for 72 hours with automated gating on error_rate and latency
Full rollout: progressive ramp to 100% over 7 days with rollback if gate thresholds breached
Post-launch: 30-day compatibility window with automatic shim and weekly migration metrics review
post_launch_checks: 24h: validate canary error rate and token cost against baseline
72h: confirm no migration regressions for top 10 customers
7d: run a quality regression sweep against internal eval prompts and alert on any accuracy drift
30d: finalize deprecation of legacy request parameter names if no regressions
launch_checklist: API contract merged and documented in public docs
SDK shims published (JS, Python, Go) and examples updated
Console dashboards created and alerting configured
Runtime kernels validated against target models and perf benchmarks attached
Security review completed and KMS integration smoke-tested
Support playbook published with troubleshooting steps and escalation path
Customer comms draft ready: release notes, migration FAQ, and email templates
Rollback runbook validated in staging with simulated incident scenarios
risks: Behavioral drift: small changes in tokenization/truncation could cause hallucination changes for chat flows
Performance regressions: new unified path may introduce extra latency in edge cases
Billing surprises: token accounting changes across shared surfaces could affect customer bills
Operational: increased alert noise if cache warmup is not tuned
mitigations: Capture and compare model outputs for a curated prompt set pre/post launch and gate on quality deltas
Add lightweight adaptive batching heuristics to prevent latency regressions under tail loads
Emit per-request cost telemetry to allow rapid reconciliation and customer follow-up
Tune cache TTLs and pre-warm critical workloads during canary
